rationale: This is a pure differencing-window parameter tweak of the archive's existing champion (Capex Ramp Funded By Research Cuts) with the same numerator logic and identical deflator, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different construction, and the three-year difference of a single-year flow variable also mixes level drift with reallocation.

A deflator swap is a minimal edit to the champion, but investment-to-capital and investment-to-sales normalizations are economically distinct (the former strips out margin/turnover heterogeneity) and the denominator is strictly positive and slow-moving, so the test is clean and interpretable even if the incremental information is modest.

Folding acquisition spending into the hard-investment budget additively rather than as a zero-inflated conditioning rank is a genuinely different specification that adjudicates between an irreversibility mechanism and a separate serial-acquirer effect, though the extreme lumpiness of DELTA(aqc) may inject tail noise that the sales-based deflator does not tame.

target_name: Composite Intangible Scaling In Research-Intensive Firms
rationale: Gross-profit-per-employee growth and gross-profit-growth-minus-plant-growth are two highly correlated measures of the same "profit growth without input growth" construct, so SUMRANK-averaging them under an unchanged gate is closer to blending two already-tested archive signals than to adding new economic content.

The framing as a conditional reversal of the published employment-growth anomaly is interesting, but the construction is contaminated: emp appears in the denominator of the gate, mechanically inducing negative dependence between the two legs, and a product of two positive ranks loads on both main effects, so the well-documented negative hiring main effect works directly against the stated positive expected sign.

The three-year low-gross-margin gate has already been paired with four different investment legs in the archive, each time delivering roughly the same -4 to -5% alpha with a near-zero Fama-MacBeth slope, which strongly suggests the alpha comes from the gate itself (a restatement of the gross profitability anomaly) rather than from the interaction being proposed here.
